principles: Visibility must not weaken fail-closed behavior.
Human progress output and JSON stdout must have separate clean contracts.
Reuse existing done_prepare flow and add the smallest safe wrapper points.
Do not redo B-783c activity-root logging work.
drivers: B-90d6 showed post-validation done_prepare silence during DONE closure projection.
The global CLI watchdog treats output as liveness, so heartbeats need independent phase deadlines.
The change touches high-risk lifecycle closeout behavior.

options.name: diagnostic-progress-with-phase-deadlines
pros: Adds real-time user visibility after validation.
Preserves fail-closed behavior by bounding every heartbeating phase.
Can be tested with focused fixtures without changing DONE gates.
cons: Requires careful stdout/stderr routing for JSON mode.
Adds some complexity around phase wrappers.

options.name: activity-log-only
pros: Reuses B-783c activity logging and avoids output changes.
cons: Does not solve real-time silence for operators.
Activity logs do not refresh terminal confidence and cannot replace progress output.
Does not address heartbeating hang safety.

options.name: remove-idle-watchdog
cons: Contradicts the execution document and reviewer audit findings.
Could hide true hangs for too long.

rationale: This option fixes the user-visible silence while preserving Proofbound fail-closed lifecycle semantics and JSON contracts.

preMortem.scenario: Heartbeat output keeps a hung closeout phase alive.
preMortem.trigger: A timer emits progress without an independent phase deadline.
preMortem.consequence: The global idle watchdog is defeated and a true hang runs until max timeout or longer.
preMortem.mitigation: Require per-phase hard deadlines and a hung-heartbeat regression smoke.

preMortem.scenario: JSON consumers break because progress pollutes stdout.
preMortem.trigger: Human progress text is written to stdout while --json is requested.
preMortem.consequence: Agents or scripts fail to parse done_prepare JSON output.
preMortem.mitigation: Route JSON-mode progress to stderr or a side channel and test stdout parseability.

preMortem.scenario: Progress output is mistaken for gate evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Messages use pass/evidence language or write lifecycle artifacts.
preMortem.consequence: Operators over-trust diagnostic output and gate separation is blurred.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep wording diagnostic-only and test that no review/DONE/Authority evidence is written by progress output.
